parts.transcript: Section 3: trainee teachers Dean and Hannah discuss a geography lesson on pencils. Lesson aims related to global interdependency (buying/selling) and transport systems (moving goods) (21/22=A,D). Problems identified: student grouping (sets of six vs pairs) and timing/pacing (23/24=B,E); materials, coordination and structure were fine. Lesson-plan flow-chart: locate the top producers on a world map (25=G); discuss pros and cons of different methods of transport (26=H); discuss countries' possible export routes to the USA (27=A); complete a worksheet about pencil distribution within the USA (28=E); share ideas about the future of pencils (29=B); prepare a talk/presentation (30=C).

parts.title: Biomass fuel
parts.transcript: Section 4: lecture on biomass fuel (briquettes from waste plant material like sawdust/straw). Benefits: no cost for materials (31); clean, easy to handle and store (32). Production by machine: biomass ground to a powder (33), then compressed and forced out through holes (34) of different shapes; only a small amount of electricity (35) is needed. Production by hand: mixed with water and sticky material e.g. starch (36), then pressed. Current use: Europe/USA for some time mainly for agriculture (37); India/China since 1990s, China had about 600 factories (38) in 2002; in Uganda customers are public institutions or businesses (39). Prospects: demand (40) is likely to increase.
